root_cause: LIVE_PROOF T-0583 (real browser + real Keycloak) found POST /api/users returns 503 for an ordinary (non-email) login: src/http/user-mgmt.ts copied `login` verbatim into kc.createHumanUser({username, email}); a real Keycloak realm rejects a non-email username/email with 400 error-invalid-email; src/keycloak/admin-port.ts's live createHumanUser folded any non-201/409 status into AUTH_UNAVAILABLE, so the route surfaced 503 'account service unavailable' for what is actually a client validation error. An email-shaped login worked (201); an ordinary login did not. The spec (docs/specs/T-0583-user-mgmt.spec.md N9) already states login=username=KC email field (mirrors register.ts), so this is honest enforcement of an existing contract, not a new field. Secondary bug: GET /api/users/accounts returned employee.slug as `login`, but slug is the KC user UUID (T-0342/T-0366 identity-resolution invariant) — the list showed a raw UUID instead of the human-readable login. Test-escape root cause: src/keycloak/fake-user-port.ts's InMemoryKeycloakUserPort never validated email format, so every unit/db test that created a user with a non-email login passed green against the fake while a real KC realm would 400 it.

fix_summary.email_validation: src/http/user-mgmt.ts validateCreateBody now rejects a non-email login with 400 VALIDATION BEFORE calling kc.createHumanUser (EMAIL_RE mirrors register.ts) — a malformed login never reaches KC. Client-side: web/src/screens/users-form.js validateCreateUser applies the same EMAIL_RE with an inline Russian field error; screen-users.jsx sets type=email on the login Field and rewords the hint from a placeholder-only hint to an explicit 'email-адрес' requirement. Defense-in-depth: src/keycloak/admin-port.ts's live createHumanUser now maps KC's 400 status to a distinct EMAIL_INVALID error code (previously silently folded into AUTH_UNAVAILABLE); user-mgmt.ts's catch block maps EMAIL_INVALID to 400 instead of the generic 503.
fix_summary.fake_fidelity: src/keycloak/fake-user-port.ts InMemoryKeycloakUserPort.createHumanUser now validates spec.email/spec.username against the same email-format regex BEFORE the failOnCreate/failOnAuth injection switches, throwing the same EMAIL_INVALID code a real Keycloak realm's 400 maps to. Proof the gap is closed: src/__tests__/fake-user-port-fidelity.test.ts creates a user with username/email='liveproof-835201' (a non-email ordinary login) directly against the fake, in isolation, with no server/DB involved, and asserts it rejects with EMAIL_INVALID — this test is RED without the fake-port fix and GREEN with it (verified by reverting the fake-port change locally and re-running: without the check, the same call resolves successfully with a fabricated userId, proving the pre-fix fake accepted what a real KC realm rejects).
fix_summary.human_readable_list: migrations/126_employee_login.sql adds an additive nullable choros.employee.login column (human-readable KC username), kept separate from the identity-bearing slug=KC-UUID (slug cannot be repurposed — org.ts resolveActorSlugFromAuth reads it as the JWT sub). src/http/user-mgmt.ts's POST /api/users INSERT now stores login into that column; GET /api/users/accounts SELECTs login and falls back to slug ONLY for rows created before this migration (dev-silo seed humans like e-kravtsova have no KC login at all, so their slug is already their sole human-readable label).
